_comment: Illustrative course-spec data for tools/doc-templates/course-pack.template.json. Trivial sample used to prove the render; not a real course. Field names are the proposed course-spec shape (gate-redesign A5); finalised in Round C.

thematicScope.priorExperienceAnchor: read an academic argument and identify its main claim

thematicStrands.label: Telling a claim from a reason
Asking what would make a claim true

courseOutcomes.text: Identify the main claim in a short argument.

confidenceStatement.text: By the end, you should feel sure you can spot the one thing an argument is trying to get you to accept.

mcqQuestions.stem: Which sentence states the author's main claim?
Which of these is a reason, not the claim itself?

courseOutcomes.text: Question whether a reason actually supports its claim.

confidenceStatement.text: You should feel able to ask, of any reason, whether it really does the work it is meant to.

mcqQuestions.stem: Which reason fails to support the claim it is attached to?

lessonMap.progression: The course moves from recognising the parts of an argument, to questioning how well they hold together, to weighing the evidence behind them. Each lesson assumes the one before it.

lessons.title: Finding the claim
lessons.topic: Telling a claim from a reason
lessons.description: You meet short arguments and learn to point to the one sentence the writer most wants you to accept.

outcomes.text: Identify the main claim in a short argument.

lessons.title: Does the reason hold?
lessons.topic: Asking what would make a claim true
lessons.description: You take a claim and its reason and ask whether the reason actually does the work it is meant to.

outcomes.text: Question whether a reason actually supports its claim.

lessons.title: Weighing the evidence
lessons.description: You look at the evidence behind a reason and judge whether it is strong enough to rely on.

outcomes.text: Judge whether the evidence given is strong or weak.
